headline: Markets brace for a hawkish Fed as AI selloff lingers
body: US equity futures are lower again heading into Wednesday's Fed decision, with Dow futures off roughly half a percent and Nasdaq futures down a similar amount as the 10-year Treasury yield pushed to 5.04%, its highest level since 2007. Sentiment around the meeting has shifted markedly hawkish: futures markets now imply somewhere near a 90% probability of a quarter-point rate hike rather than a cut, a sharp reversal from earlier-year expectations, as officials weigh a stronger-than-expected August jobs report and inflation still running near 3% against a slowing-growth backdrop. The combination of rising real yields and a central bank leaning toward tightening rather than easing is compressing risk appetite broadly, with rate-sensitive and long-duration growth names bearing the brunt of the pressure heading into tomorrow's announcement.

The bigger story of the week remains the fallout from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's essay calling for a deliberate slowdown in frontier AI development, echoed by OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk. The message hit the AI-infrastructure trade hard on Monday — chipmakers and AI-capex names sold off sharply — while capital rotated into cybersecurity and enterprise-software names seen as beneficiaries of more cautious AI deployment, with names like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks posting double-digit gains. That rotation is still working through the market today rather than reversing. Retail-sentiment trackers mostly show attention concentrated on the same semiconductor and AI names already driving headlines rather than any distinct social-media narrative, so today's read leans more on this policy-and-positioning story than on fresh crowd chatter.
